Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Light Up a Life 2026

Hilary Gotts asked on here last week whether we are doing the tree again this year. Yes, Hilary, we are, and please do bring your sister.

For anyone who hasn't seen it before, every winter we put a tree in the shop window and hang it with memory tags, each one carrying the name of somebody who is missed. Last year there were 412. I read a good many of them while I was dusting round the window, and I want to thank everyone who trusted us with a name. Between you, you also helped the hospice keep its night sitters going, and I know there are families reading this who could tell you what that meant.

Here are this year's arrangements.

Memory tags will be in the shop from Monday 16 November. The suggested donation is £3. If you would rather write yours at home, there are envelopes on the counter to take away with you.

We switch the lights on on Saturday 28 November at 4pm. The Gildencroft Primary choir are coming back to sing three or four carols, and Doreen is making her mince pies again. Going by last year, I would not arrive late if you want one.

Every name on the tree will be read out at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm, in the day centre. You are very welcome to come, but you don't have to be there for your name to be read.

My husband Ray died at the hospice in November 2019, so it is seven years this month. The first year I hung his tag I could hardly write it. Now I write it at the counter in the shop, with the same pen. I only mention it because some of you will be writing a tag for the first time this year, and I remember what that was like.

The tree is for anyone who is grieving. You don't need to have had someone at the hospice, and it doesn't matter whether it was last month or forty years ago. If there is somebody you miss, there is room for their name.

And you don't need to buy anything, or write anything either. If you would just like to come in and stand by the tree for a few minutes, please do. Nobody will ask you what you're looking for.

Thank you, as always, for remembering with us.

Jean
